messages:
Avery (Billing): Quick heads-up — starting 2026-06-15 00:00 UTC we’re simplifying the pricing matrix and introducing an overnight burst allowance for low-traffic windows. Details below and an FAQ will go live later today. 
Avery (Billing): High-level changes: 
• Three SKU bands (H, M, L) replaces per-route micro-tiers.
• Invoice granularity moves to per-minute metering (instead of per-hour) for token compute.
• Overnight burst: 00:00-06:00 UTC gets a soft burst pool that won’t immediately trigger overage flags.
• Legacy free starter credits: phased sunset with a 90-day wind-down and an opt-in migration for qualifying startups.
Avery (Billing): Why: simplify cost predictability and reduce noisy hourly blips that cause invoices and alerts to spike.
Morgan (Finance): Effective date? and will we prorate for mid-month changes?
Avery (Billing): Effective 2026-06-15. We’ll prorate only for customers on reserved commitments (Dedicated). Hosted usage switches per-minute on cutover; invoices will include a clear delta line item for the first billing cycle.
Devon (Eng Ops): Any API/SDK breaking changes? rate-limit headers changing?
Avery (Billing): No breaking changes. We’re adding an optional header X-Redwood-Rate-Band to responses for visibility. SDKs will pick this up in next patch but older clients continue to work.
billing-bot: Example invoice snippet for hosted usage (first cycle):
```
Line item: Token compute - old hourly model: $123.45
Line item: Token compute - new per-minute model: $118.97
Delta: -$4.48 (applied as credit on first invoice)
Overage Alerts: suppressed for burst window 00:00-06:00 UTC for small bursts (<5% of monthly baseline)
```
Sana (Support): We’ll need email templates + FAQ. Can you share the migration checklist for support?
Avery (Billing): Yes — templates and an internal playbook will be published to the docs repo this afternoon. I’ll ping here with the doc link.
Morgan (Finance): How does the overnight burst interact with rate limiting? Could behavior be abused by global customers?
Avery (Billing): Burst is a soft policy: it relaxes overage alarms and allows a temporary spike, but it does not remove throttling. Abuse detection still applies (anomaly detection + rate-of-change heuristics). High sustained usage will still hit standard limits and be routed to burst-exhaustion fallback models.
Devon (Eng Ops): Need to flag any SLO changes for Dedicated customers. Can we schedule a sync with Product & SRE?
Avery (Billing): Yes — 1pm PT tomorrow for a 30m sync. Invites going out now.
Sana (Support): For legacy free credits: timeline? customers asking today already.
Avery (Billing): Legacy starter credits remain usable through 2026-08-15. After that, remaining balance converts to a one-time invoice credit applied over the following 30 days. Eligible startups can request a one-time extension (apply form will be in the FAQ).
Morgan (Finance): Any expected net revenue delta estimate? rough numbers fine.
Avery (Billing): Early sims show a ~1-3% revenue uplift from banding and per-minute accuracy in year-1; but lower churn risk from fewer surprise invoices. We’ll publish the model in the finance note.
Devon (Eng Ops): I’ll validate monitoring dashboards for the new header and burst windows.
Avery (Billing): Thanks — appreciate it. I’ll post the FAQ link in ~2h and update here when the doc is live. :megaphone:
billing-bot: Internal doc created: /docs/billing/pricing-matrix-2026-cutover (draft)
Sana (Support): Got it, we’ll queue the canned replies.
Morgan (Finance): Approved for announcement to customers after internal docs + FAQ live.
Avery (Billing): Great — publishing to marketing & status pages after the doc is posted. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
